assumptions.condition: \(a\mapsto E_P[Y(a)\mid X=x]\in C(I)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).

standard.name: continuous-treatment overlap on an interior interval

definitions.name: \(\mathcal M\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M=\{P:P\text{ satisfies every condition indexed by }\mathrm{by\_member\_properties}\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathscr D_n\) and \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\)
definitions.construction: For a candidate law \(Q\in\mathcal M\), let \(F_{x,Q}\), \(G_{x,Q}\), and \(p_{x,Q}\) denote its channels and stratum masses, and set \(\mathscr D_n(Q)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\{\int_{\mathcal C_*}(|\widehat F_{x,n}-F_{x,Q}|^2+B_Y^{-2}|\widehat G_{x,n}-G_{x,Q}|^2)\,ds\,dt+|\widehat p_x-p_{x,Q}|^2\}\) and \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}=\{Q\in\mathcal M:\mathscr D_n(Q)\le\epsilon_n^2\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}\)
definitions.construction: Apply order-\(K_n\) Taylor--Legendre outer enclosures to \(\varphi_{f,x}\) and \(\varphi_{q,x}\), truncate each error law by its second-moment tail envelope, replace each truncated law by positive atomic quadrature exact through order \(2K_n\), and run outward-rounded Bernstein interval branch-and-bound on \(\mathcal C_*\times I\) until every objective and constraint enclosure has radius at most \(\zeta_n\); \(\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}\) is the finite set of retained rational coefficient, quadrature, tail, and remainder boxes with their outward interval certificates.

definitions.name: \(\operatorname{Dec}_n\) and \(\Theta^{\mathrm{cert}}_{n,\alpha}\)
definitions.construction: For each \(b\in\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}\), define \(\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\) as the set of all full laws \(Q\in\mathcal M\) whose stratum masses, order-\(K_n\) Taylor--Legendre coefficients of their latent-density and marked-density transforms, positive order-\(2K_n\) error quadratures, second-moment tail components, and certified analytic remainders lie in the corresponding coordinate and remainder intervals of \(b\), and whose exact paired-channel discrepancy satisfies the outward constraint interval recorded by \(b\). Set \(\Theta^{\mathrm{cert}}_{n,\alpha}=\bigcup_{b\in\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}}\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\subseteq\mathcal M\).

definitions.name: \(J_{b,n}(a)\), \(\underline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n\), and \(\overline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n\)
definitions.construction: For \(b\in\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}\) and \(a\in I\), let \(J_{b,n}(a)\) be the outward-rounded interval evaluation of \(\mu_Q(a)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_{x,Q}q_{x,Q}(a)/f_{x,Q}(a)\) over all coordinates and certified remainders in \(b\), with the denominator interval intersected with \([\kappa,\infty)\). If \(\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}\neq\varnothing\), set \(\underline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)=\min_{b\in\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}}\inf J_{b,n}(a)\) and \(\overline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)=\max_{b\in\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}}\sup J_{b,n}(a)\); otherwise set both evaluations to zero.

definitions.name: \(L_n\) and \(U_n\)
definitions.construction: If \(\Theta^{\mathrm{cert}}_{n,\alpha}\neq\varnothing\), the decoded-law profile endpoints \(\inf_{Q\in\Theta^{\mathrm{cert}}_{n,\alpha}}\mu_Q(a)\) and \(\sup_{Q\in\Theta^{\mathrm{cert}}_{n,\alpha}}\mu_Q(a)\) are evaluated outward by \(\underline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)\) and \(\overline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)\), and set \(L_n(a)=\max\{-B_Y,\underline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)-\zeta_n\}\) and \(U_n(a)=\min\{B_Y,\overline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)+\zeta_n\}\); if \(\Theta^{\mathrm{cert}}_{n,\alpha}=\varnothing\), set \(L_n(a)=U_n(a)=0\) for every \(a\in I\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}=\{(L_n,U_n):L_n,U_n\text{ are jointly measurable},\ L_n\le U_n,\ \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(L_n(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for all }a\in I)\ge1-\alpha\}\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{up}}\)
definitions.construction: Use the continuous integrated probability and signed marked contrasts on \(\mathcal C_*\), derive a nearly parametric forward radius, pass both entire transforms through one quantitative analytic-continuation argument at order \(K_n\), recover \(q_x/f_x\) on \(I\), and certify the resulting outer profile by outward-rounded Taylor--Legendre and Bernstein interval enclosures.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{low}}\)
definitions.construction: Freeze \(p_x\), \(f_x=f^{\circ}\), and two nonidentical asymmetric error laws; relocate the compact-support Legendre moment-annihilating packet from the latent density to a Bernoulli conditional mark, preserve strict \(H^{\beta}\) slack and the Bernoulli range, retain factorial attenuation in the observed marked channel, and apply the confidence-band testing reduction.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \((s,t)\in\mathbb R^2\), \(F_x(s,t)=p_x\varphi_{f,x}(s+t)\varphi_1(s)\varphi_2(t)\) and \(G_x(s,t)=p_x\varphi_{q,x}(s+t)\varphi_1(s)\varphi_2(t)\); moreover \(\inf_{|u|\le\nu_*}|\varphi_j(u)|\ge1/2\) for \(j\in\{1,2\}\).
statements.justification: The common nuisance factor makes the probability and marked channels comparable on one protected cube, while the moment bound derives protection rather than assuming it.
statements.gap: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy derive the unmarked factorization; the signed outcome-marked factorization and its joint use for a causal quotient are not part of their result.
statements.consumer: The paired factorization is the input to the sharp inverse modulus and to every computable profile restriction.

statements.statement: The observed law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) identifies \(p_x\), \(f_x\), and \(q_x\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), and for every \(a\in I\) it identifies the causal curve by \(\mu(a)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(a)/f_x(a)\).
statements.justification: The theorem separates the qualitative causal identifying step from the quantitative band-width problem.
statements.gap: Huang and Zhang identify the ADRF with a known error transform, while Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy identify only an unmarked latent signal under blind replicates.
statements.consumer: Applied analyses with replicate dietary or exposure measurements obtain a whole-curve causal target before inference is imposed.

statements.statement: There is a constant \(C_{\alpha}\) depending only on the fixed class constants such that, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(\mathscr D_n(P)\le\epsilon_n^2)\ge1-\alpha\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).
statements.justification: Continuous integrated control is the stochastic replacement for the refuted empirical-frequency grid.
statements.gap: Kato, Sasaki, and Ura control finitely many self-normalized complex moments; the present claim controls both marked and unmarked channels continuously over a fixed square.
statements.consumer: The result supplies a coverage-valid continuous feasible profile without assuming between-grid transform behavior.

statements.statement: Establish constants \(c,C>0\) such that, for all sufficiently small \(\delta>0\), any \(P,Q\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \(\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\{\int_{\mathcal C_*}(|F_{x,P}-F_{x,Q}|^2+B_Y^{-2}|G_{x,P}-G_{x,Q}|^2)\,ds\,dt+|p_{x,P}-p_{x,Q}|^2\}\le\delta^2\) obey \(\|\mu_P-\mu_Q\|_{L^\infty(I)}\le C\{\log\log(1/\delta)/\log(1/\delta)\}^{\beta-1/2}\), with the exponent unimprovable on a fixed-density, fixed-error Bernoulli-marked submodel.
statements.justification: This quantitative modulus is the genuinely open bridge from nearly parametric forward control to the proposed sharp causal sup-norm width.
statements.gap: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy prove an unmarked \(L^2\) density modulus; no result gives the paired marked-channel \(L^\infty\) quotient modulus or freezes all unmarked nuisances in the converse.
statements.consumer: Resolving the question turns blind replicate information into an explicit sample-size requirement for simultaneous ADRF precision.

statements.statement: There exists \(C<\infty\) such that the certified finite-profile algorithm terminates for every sample and returns \(\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}\) with \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\subseteq\Theta^{\mathrm{cert}}_{n,\alpha}=\bigcup_{b\in\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}}\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\subseteq\mathcal M\). For every \(a\in I\) and \(b\in\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}\), \(\{\mu_Q(a):Q\in\operatorname{Dec}_n(b)\}\subseteq J_{b,n}(a)\). Whenever \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\neq\varnothing\), the outward endpoint evaluations satisfy \(0\le\inf_{Q\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_Q(a)-\underline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)\le C\zeta_n\) and \(0\le\overline m^{\mathrm{cert}}_n(a)-\sup_{Q\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}\mu_Q(a)\le C\zeta_n=o(r_n)\), uniformly over \(a\in I\). Moreover, \(|\mathscr B_{n,\alpha}|\le\exp\{C K_n^2\log(K_n/\zeta_n)\}\).
statements.justification: Honesty is operational only if every continuum restriction and endpoint is enclosed by a checkable finite certificate.
statements.gap: Kato, Sasaki, and Ura implement a finite frequency inversion but do not certify equivalence to a continuum profile; Neumann uses a continuous metric without a finite outer optimization.
statements.consumer: Empirical users obtain reproducible band endpoints whose numerical error is asymptotically negligible relative to statistical width.

statements.statement: There exists \(C<\infty\) such that the certified profiled band \((L_n,U_n)\) belongs to \(\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\) and satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]\le C r_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).
statements.justification: This is the constructive half of the simultaneous-band frontier and includes the numerical certificate in the inferential object.
statements.gap: Colangelo and Lee provide uniform-in-treatment ADRF inference when treatment is measured without error, while Huang and Zhang provide pointwise inference with a known error transform; neither confronts blind asymmetric-replicate deconvolution, and existing deconvolution bands target a density or regression under auxiliary or symmetric error information.
statements.consumer: Nutrition and pollution studies with two nonidentical replicate measurements can report a uniformly valid ADRF band with an interpretable worst-case width.

statements.statement: There exist \(c>0\) and \(P_{0,n},P_{1,n}\in\mathcal M\) with the same \(p_x\), the same \(f_x=f^{\circ}\), and the same two fixed nonidentical asymmetric error laws, such that \(Y\mid(A=a,X=x)\) is Bernoulli under both laws, \(\|\mu_{1,n}-\mu_{0,n}\|_{L^\infty(I)}\ge c r_n\), and \(\|P_{1,n,\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}-P_{0,n,\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\eta\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).
statements.justification: Freezing the entire unmarked replicate law isolates ADRF uncertainty and prevents the lower bound from being driven by latent-density estimation.
statements.gap: The lower experiment of Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy changes the latent density and separates in \(L^2\); Lounici and Nickl likewise perturb the deconvolved density rather than a bounded outcome mark.
statements.consumer: The construction certifies that no honest causal band can evade the logarithmic width by estimating the design density or error laws more accurately.

statements.statement: There exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that \(c r_n\le\mathfrak R_n\le C r_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\); equivalently, \(\mathfrak R_n\asymp\{\log\log n/\log n\}^{\beta-1/2}\).
statements.justification: The matching expected-maximal-width frontier is the theorem-level statistical contribution.
statements.gap: No cited work matches an honest ADRF sup-band upper bound to a fixed-nuisance marked lower bound under fully blind asymmetric replicates with spectral zeros.
statements.consumer: Study designers can translate the frontier into sample-size calculations for resolving clinically or economically meaningful dose-response features.

statements.statement: On the submodel \(U_1=U_2=0\) almost surely, the factorization becomes \(F_x(s,t)=p_x\varphi_{f,x}(s+t)\) and \(G_x(s,t)=p_x\varphi_{q,x}(s+t)\), while the identified ADRF remains \(\mu(a)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xE_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\), the standard continuous-treatment g-formula.
statements.justification: The reduction checks that the blind-replicate construction preserves the established causal target when measurement error vanishes.
statements.gap: The result is a required sanity reduction rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: Implementations can be unit-tested against the ordinary error-free ADRF functional.

sampling_model.design: I.i.d. superpopulation sampling from a fixed finite-stratum law.
sampling_model.treatment: The latent dose \(A_i\) is observed only through \(S_{i1}=A_i+U_{i1}\) and \(S_{i2}=A_i+U_{i2}\); the errors are independent, nonidentically distributed, potentially asymmetric, and may have characteristic-function zero sets.
sampling_model.overlap: The finite strata have masses at least \(p_{\min}\), and \(f_x(a)\ge\kappa\) on \(I\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The probability and signed marked channels are controlled by continuous integrated empirical contrasts on \(\mathcal C_*\). Entire-transform continuation and Sobolev recovery are profiled jointly, and an outward-rounded finite certificate approximates every continuum constraint to \(\zeta_n=o(r_n)\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The compact-support blind-replicate density estimator attains squared \(L^2\) risk of order \((\log\log n/\log n)^{2\beta}\), with a matching density lower bound.
The known-error continuous-treatment estimator admits pointwise asymptotic inference for the ADRF.

Theorems S11 and S12 give a uniform-in-treatment asymptotically linear representation and multiplier-bootstrap inference for the ADRF when the continuous treatment is observed without measurement error.
A latent-variable variational framework estimates a continuous-treatment ADRF under measurement error with neural density models.
Inverting finite complex Kotlarski moment tests gives a uniformly size-controlled latent-density confidence band without imposing completeness.
A multiplier-bootstrap density band is uniformly valid when the unknown error law is learned from auxiliary data or symmetric repeated measurements.
Wavelet deconvolution estimators attain minimax sup-norm density rates under a known convolution operator.
Testing affinity yields lower bounds on confidence-band width over nonparametric function classes.
Under weak unconfoundedness and positivity, the error-free ADRF is identified by the continuous-treatment g-formula.

tldr: The observed law contains two bilinear transform channels: an unmarked probability channel and an outcome-marked signed channel. Continuous integrated control of both channels on a moment-derived protected frequency square, followed by quantitative analytic continuation and Sobolev recovery, is conjectured to yield an honest simultaneous band for the ADRF with expected maximal width \(r_n\asymp(\log\log n/\log n)^{\beta-1/2}\). A terminating outward-rounded finite profile decodes rational certificate boxes into sets of full laws and evaluates their ADRFs by certified intervals, making the band operational without an empirical-grid inverse. A fixed-density, fixed-error Bernoulli marked experiment supplies the matching lower bound and isolates uncertainty about the causal curve rather than uncertainty about the treatment density.

project_justification.gap: Colangelo and Lee give uniform-in-treatment ADRF inference when treatment is measured without error, and known-error measurement-error methods give pointwise ADRF inference. Blind repeated-measurement methods identify and estimate an unmarked density, and robust Kotlarski methods invert finite complex moments for density bands. None gives an honest whole-curve ADRF band, a sharp expected-width modulus, or a fixed-nuisance marked converse when the two replicate errors are unknown, asymmetric, nonidentical, and allowed to have spectral zeros.
project_justification.niche: Compact dose support makes both the density transform and the signed marked transform entire. A common second-moment radius supplies a uniform nonvanishing neighborhood by \(|\varphi_j(t)|\ge1-|t|\sqrt{M_e}\), so the protected square is derived from a standard moment condition. The inferential object is a paired nonlinear quotient rather than a single density inverse.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the paired protected inverse at the sharp sup-norm exponent, embeds it in a continuously constrained confidence profile, decodes every retained rational box into represented full laws, certifies the resulting law-valued profile endpoints by outward interval evaluation with negligible inflation, and matches the upper width with Bernoulli marked alternatives that leave the full unmarked replicate law fixed.

related_work: Colangelo and Lee (2025), especially Supplementary Theorems S11 and S12 on pages 63--65 of the public manuscript, are the closest published uniform-in-treatment ADRF comparator: they derive a uniform asymptotically linear representation and multiplier-bootstrap inference over a compact treatment set when treatment is measured without error. Thus whole-curve ADRF inference itself is not the new obstacle; the obstacle is simultaneous inference after blind deconvolution with two unknown, nonidentical, asymmetric replicate errors. Huang and Zhang (2023) motivate the continuous-treatment measurement-error problem and derive pointwise ADRF inference when the error transform is known; their operator is not blind and their result is not simultaneous. Gao, Bondell, Huang, and Gong (2024) estimate a latent-treatment ADRF through a variational neural model, without a blind-replicate identification or honest-band theorem. Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy (2025) provide the closest method exemplar: their continuous integrated analytic-polynomial contrast achieves a nearly parametric local transform error, analytic continuation yields an unmarked density rate, and a Legendre packet proves a compact-support density converse. The present target adds a signed marked channel, a quotient, supremum loss, honest band coverage, and a fixed-nuisance lower experiment. Kato, Sasaki, and Ura (2021) show how test inversion avoids fragile closed-form Kotlarski division, but their finite moments target an unmarked density and do not certify a continuum profile or a sharp width. Kato and Sasaki (2018, 2019) supply Gaussian and multiplier-bootstrap machinery for density and errors-in-variables regression bands under auxiliary, symmetric, or conventional spectral information. Neumann (2007) motivates integrated characteristic functions as continuous probability coordinates. Lounici and Nickl (2011), Genovese and Wasserman (2008), and Low (1997) inform the sup-norm packing and band-width reduction. The Colangelo--Lee comparison is informed-by rather than a claimed tightening; the only equivalence claim is the explicit error-free reduction in Theorem 9.
technical_internal_limitation: The protected inverse in Open-ended Question 4 is load-bearing. Its proof must keep the continuous forward error nearly parametric while analytic continuation amplifies only the stochastic error; inserting a spatial Jackson remainder into the forward tolerance recreates the rejected parent argument. The finite certificate must enclose the continuum constraints directly and may have pessimistic worst-case complexity. On the lower side, the same packet must preserve the Bernoulli range, strict Sobolev slack, fixed nuisance laws, and product-law total variation; failure of any one condition invalidates the claimed frontier.
honest_scope: The main frontier fixes \(\beta\), the support interval, all Sobolev radii, overlap constants, the outcome bound, and a common error second-moment radius. Error distributions remain unknown, nonidentical, asymmetric, and may have zero sets away from the moment-derived protected neighborhood. Adaptation to unknown smoothness or drifting channel severity is outside the theorem. When \(U_1=U_2=0\), Theorem 9 recovers the standard error-free g-formula.

seed_details.red_team: A cynical referee could call the result the compact-support density theorem followed by Sobolev embedding.

novelty_justification: Colangelo and Lee (2025), Supplementary Theorems S11 and S12, settle uniform-in-treatment ADRF inference when treatment is correctly measured, so whole-curve inference alone is not the novelty. The closest inverse-problem theorem-level anchor proves a compact-support minimax rate for an unmarked latent density in squared \(L^2\) loss. The proposed kernel changes the first proof step: it estimates two continuous integrated channels, analytically continues both, and recovers the denominator-stabilized marked quotient in supremum norm under blind asymmetric replicates. This produces the exponent \(\beta-1/2\), not the anchor's density exponent \(\beta\). The upper result is an honest whole-curve confidence band whose semi-infinite profile is replaced by a terminating outward certificate: each rational box is decoded as a set of full laws, and interval evaluation gives \(o(r_n)\) endpoint inflation. The lower result freezes every unmarked nuisance and moves only a valid Bernoulli conditional mark, so the all-band lower bound isolates causal-curve uncertainty. The exact target--method pair is not occupied by the measurement-error-free uniform ADRF literature, known-error pointwise ADRF literature, auxiliary-error density-band literature, robust Kotlarski inversion literature, or blind unmarked deconvolution literature.
